propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of Officer's May 1, 2020 decision denying permanent residence on H and C grounds under subsection 25(1) of the Act
propositions.quote: Ms. Jasmine Curleitha Charles (the “Applicant”) seeks judicial review of the decision made by an Officer (the “Officer”), on or about May 1, 2020, denying her request to seek permanent residence from within Canada on Humanitarian and Compassionate (“H and C”) grounds, pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c. 27 (the “Act”).

paragraphs.summary: Applicant seeks judicial review of Officer's May 1, 2020 decision denying permanent residence on H and C grounds under subsection 25(1) of the Act, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant is citizen of St. Vincent and the Grenadines, entered Canada as visitor in 1999, mother of Canadian-born child in 2013
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of St. Vincent and the Grenadines. She entered Canada as a visitor on February 26, 1999 and has remained since that day. She is a mother of a child who was born in Canada in 2013.

propositions.text: Applicant based H and C application on establishment in Canada and best interests of her child, among other things
propositions.quote: She based her H and C application on her establishment in Canada and the best interests of her child, among other things.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is citizen of St. Vincent and mother of Canadian-born child; based H and C application on establishment and child's best interests, court states.

propositions.text: Officer's decision is reviewable on reasonableness standard per Canada v. Vavilov (2019)
propositions.quote: The Officer’s decision is reviewable on the standard of reasonableness, pursuant to the decision in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov (2019), 441 D.L.R. (4th) 1 (S.C.C.).

paragraphs.summary: Officer's decision is reviewable on reasonableness standard per Canada v. Vavilov (2019), court states.

propositions.text: Officer's decision is unreasonable regarding establishment and best interests of Canadian-born child
propositions.quote: The Applicant argues that the Officer’s decision is unreasonable, in particular with respect to the elements of establishment and the best interests of her Canadian-born child.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer's decision is unreasonable on establishment and child's best interests, applicant submits.

propositions.quote: The Minister of Citizenship and Immigration (the “Respondent”) submits that the decision is reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits the decision is reasonable, respondent argues.

propositions.text: Not satisfied decision is reasonable; judicial intervention warranted
propositions.quote: Upon reading the materials filed and hearing the submissions of Counsel, I am not satisfied that the decision is reasonable. Judicial intervention in this matter is warranted.

paragraphs.summary: Court is not satisfied decision is reasonable and finds judicial intervention warranted, court concludes.

propositions.text: Officer unreasonably used Applicant's lack of status since 1999 to assess establishment in Canada
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the Officer unreasonably used the fact that the Applicant stayed in Canada since 1999 without status, in assessing her establishment in Canada since that time.

propositions.text: Failure to regularize immigration status is not per se a factor minimizing establishment; see Mitchell v. Canada (2019 FC 190)
propositions.quote: The failure to regularize immigration status is not, per se, a factor that minimizes a person’s establishing in Canada; see the decision in Mitchell v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2019 FC 190.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer unreasonably used Applicant's lack of status to assess establishment; cites Mitchell v. Canada that status failure alone doesn't minimize establishment.

propositions.text: Officer unreasonably found limited evidence of establishment; conclusion unsupported by evidence
propositions.quote: The Officer also unreasonably found that there was limited evidence of establishment. This conclusion is not supported by the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer unreasonably found limited evidence of establishment unsupported by evidence, court states.

propositions.text: Officer erred in assessing best interests of Canadian-born child by dismissing child's life in Canada
propositions.quote: In my view, the Officer further erred in her assessment of the best interests of the Applicant’s Canadian-born child by apparently dismissing the fact that the child has spent his life in Canada.

propositions.text: Officer did not engage with best interests of Canadian-born child
propositions.quote: I agree with the submissions of the Applicant that the Officer did not engage with the best interests of the Canadian-born child.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer erred by dismissing child's life in Canada; agrees with Applicant that Officer failed to engage with child's best interests.

propositions.text: Officer's reasons show misguided approach to child's best interests assessment
propositions.quote: The following quotation from the Officer’s reasons demonstrates a misguided approach to assessment of the child’s best interests: … While I have considered that remaining united in Canada with his mother would be ideal, I am not persuaded that a return to St. Vincent would seriously harm the child’s best interests. I am mindful that the child will retain his Canadian citizenship regardless of where he resides and thus will be afforded all the rights and opportunities available to other Canadian citizens. I find it is in the best interests of the child to remain united with his mother regardless of geographical location.

paragraphs.summary: Court quotes Officer's reasons showing misguided approach to child's best interests assessment, court states.

propositions.text: H and C discretion must be exercised reasonably with fair assessment, not mechanically to deny
propositions.quote: While an H and C application involves the exercise of discretion by the Respondent and his agents and delegates, that discretion is to be exercised reasonably with a fair assessment of the personal circumstances of an applicant and not in a mechanical manner, seeking a way to deny an application.

paragraphs.summary: Court states H and C discretion must be exercised reasonably with fair assessment, not mechanically to deny, court explains law.

propositions.text: No need to address other Applicant arguments
propositions.quote: It is not necessary for me to address the other arguments raised by the Applicant.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no need to address other Applicant arguments, court states.

propositions.text: Judicial review allowed; Officer's decision set aside; matter remitted to different officer for redetermination; no certification question
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review will be allowed, the decision of the Officer will be set aside and the matter remitted to a different officer for redetermination. There is no question for certification arising. JUDGMENT in IMM-2437-20 THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is allowed, the decision of the Officer is set aside and the matter is remitted to a different officer for redetermination. There is no question for certification arising.

paragraphs.summary: Court allows judicial review, sets aside Officer's decision, remits matter to different officer, no certification question, court orders.
